The concept of emotion preference was first proposed in EmoPrefer, playing a crucial role in training reward models capable of understanding human emotions. We employ the weighted F1-score (WAF) as the primary metric and accuracy (ACC) as the secondary metric. This is part of the MER2026 Challenge at ACM Multimedia 2026.

pages.title: overview
pages.content:
MER-Prefer: Emotion Preference

MER-Prefer is a newly introduced track. The concept of emotion preference was first proposed in EmoPrefer, which predicts which of two emotion descriptions is preferred by human annotators for a given video. This task plays a crucial role in training reward models capable of understanding human emotions.

We provide two training datasets: EmoPrefer-Data with majority-voted labels and EmoPrefer-Data-V2 with single-annotator labels. For testing, we provide 379 samples with majority-voted labels.

See the baseline paper for more details: https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.19417

Official website: https://zeroqiaoba.github.io/MER-Challenge/

Submission Format

The result file must be named answer.csv with the following columns:

  • name: sample identifier
  • a1: first emotion description (text)
  • a2: second emotion description (text)
  • preference: the preferred description — must be exactly a1 or a2

Compress answer.csv into answer.zip and submit via Codabench.

Important Updates from the Organizing Committee Dear MER2026 Participants and Colleagues, Thank you for your continuous support and active participation in the MER2026 challenge. To ensure fairness, robust evaluation, and transparency, the Organizing Committee is issuing important updates regarding the evaluation protocols, specifically for Track 3, as well as overarching rules on method validity. Please review the following information carefully, as it impacts final rankings and submission guidelines. 1. Track 3 (MER-Prefer) Evaluation Updates & Leaderboard Statement To better assess model robustness, the final ranking for Track 3 will now be determined by the average score of Stage 1 (the current test set) and Stage 2 (a supplementary test set).
  • Stage 2 Release:The Stage 2 test set will be released on July 11, AoE.
  • Submission Limit:Each team is allowed strictly ONE submission for Stage 2. A dedicated submission channel will be provided shortly.
  • Deadline:The final submission deadline remains unchanged at July 13, AoE.

Regarding the Current Leaderboard: In response to the exceptionally high accuracy scores on the current Codabench leaderboard, the committee has initiated a technical verification process of the relevant pipelines. The current results remain valid pending this review. Until a definitive conclusion is reached, there is no evidence of misconduct. We kindly urge all participants to remain objective and refrain from spreading unverified speculation that could harm the reputation of individuals or teams.

Post-Competition Reproducibility: After the competition, the first-place team in Track 3 will be required to publicly release fully reproducible materials (e.g., via GitHub), including code, training/testing scripts, model configurations, and instructions. These materials will be open for community review to ensure absolute transparency.

2. Method Validity and Reproducibility (Applicable to All Tracks) All final submissions must be generated by a learnable, reproducible, and generalizable modeling pipeline.
  • Acceptable Practices:Teams may use reasonable preprocessing methods, priors derived from training samples, or components that aid in learning generalizable structures, provided they are part of a complete and auditable pipeline.
  • Prohibited Shortcuts:Submissions must not rely on non-generalizable, competition-specific shortcuts. This includes using sample identifiers (sample_idis strictly an index, not a semantic feature), file naming conventions, test sample ordering, fixed lookups, manual scaling, constant biases, or rules calibrated repeatedly via leaderboard feedback. If priors or calibration terms from training data are used, teams must clearly explain their role and demonstrate their contribution via ablation studies.
  • Format Compliance:All submissions must strictly adhere to the official starting_kitregarding templates, entry functions, file organization, and output formats.
3. Compliance Audits and Verification The organizing committee will conduct random checks during and after the competition. If a submission displays abnormal performance, highly unusual historical fluctuations, or suggests over-reliance on fixed priors or manual calibrations, the committee will contact the team for proof of reproducibility. To verify your methods, you may be required to provide:
  • Trained model weights and source code.
  • Training/inference scripts and configuration files.
  • Random seeds and preprocessing/inference instructions.
  • Ablation study results.
Failure to prove that a submission originates from a legitimate, reproducible pipeline, or the discovery of prohibited shortcuts, will result in the submission being deemed invalid and excluded from the final rankings.
The committee sincerely apologizes for any confusion these rule clarifications and reviews may cause. We are committed to protecting the legitimate rights of all participants while upholding the integrity of the challenge. Thank you for your understanding and cooperation. Best regards, MER2026 Organizing Committee

pages.title: evaluation
pages.content:
Evaluation

In MER-Prefer, we evaluate two-class preference classification using Weighted F1-score (WAF) as the primary metric and Accuracy (ACC) as the secondary metric.

For each sample, the submission must predict whether description a1 or a2 is preferred by human annotators. The prediction is evaluated against the ground truth preference labels.

The submission must contain exactly 10,000 samples. Only samples whose (name, a1, a2) tuple exists in the ground truth set are evaluated.

See the baseline paper for more details: https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.19417

Official website: https://zeroqiaoba.github.io/MER-Challenge/
pages.content_zh:
评估

在MER-Prefer中，我们使用加权F1分数（WAF）作为主要评估指标，准确率（ACC）作为次要评估指标来评估二分类偏好分类。

对于每个样本，提交内容必须预测人类标注员更倾向于描述a1还是a2。预测结果将与真实的偏好标签进行比较。

提交内容必须包含恰好10,000个样本。仅评估其(name, a1, a2)元组存在于真实数据集中的样本。

详见基准论文：https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.19417

官方网站：https://zeroqiaoba.github.io/MER-Challenge/
